thread:
Maria Chen: :rotating_light: I'm seeing a sustained spike in requests to /v1/embeddings from a small set of IP ranges, starting ~15m ago. Error rates are low but we're hitting token throughput limits and causing tail latency for paying customers. CPU on embedding workers is pegged in us-west-1.

incident-bot: page sent to #incidents oncall @ryan (priority: high) — incident created: 1951234567

Ryan Patel: I'm on it, grabbing logs and IPs. Maria, can you share top 10 source IPs and any UA strings?

Maria Chen: top IPs: 44.210.11.5, 44.210.11.7, 3.120.55.6, 18.204.33.99, 51.15.72.4. UA looks like "python-requests/2.28" + lots of custom headers. Volume looks like repeated small requests (batch_size=1) across many keys.

Jamal Ortiz: Sounds like a credential-spraying / scraper farm. Are these keys new? Any spikes in key creation?

Maria Chen: Checking now — several keys created 2–3 days ago from same org; but there's also high traffic from keys that are weeks old. Rate per key is low but fanout is wide.

Sofia Rivera: Support Pager: we have 3 customer tickets about slow embedding responses in last 10m, one high-priority on-call customer affected.

Ryan Patel: Immediate plan: 1) Apply temporary stricter per-key QPS and per-minute token quota for embedding route. 2) Deploy WAF rule to block known bad UA + fingerprint. 3) Geo-shape for offending IP ranges (throttle to 1r/s). 4) Notify affected customers. Anyone object?

Maria Chen: +1, do steps in that order. We should keep canary so we don't affect legitimate traffic.

Jamal Ortiz: I'll take WAF and rate-limit rules. Ryan, can you do the quota changes?

Ryan Patel: On it. Applying per-key cap to 5 r/s and per-minute token cap to 5k tokens for embeddings on keys that match suspicious activity.

-- commands --
Ryan Patel: Running: 
```
# pseudo commands
curl -X POST https://console.api/redwood/admin/keys/quota -d '{"filter":"suspicious","qps":5,"token_per_min":5000}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

Ryan Patel: Quota API returned 202. Applying rollback watch for 10m.

Jamal Ortiz: WAF rule: block UA regex "python-requests|curl/7|scrapy" and add rate limit on path /v1/embeddings, scope=IP.

-- commands --
Jamal Ortiz: WAF API: 
```
POST /waf/rules
{"name":"scraper-ua-block-195123","condition":{"any":[{"ua_regex":"python-requests"},{"ua_regex":"scrapy"}]},"action":"block","scope":"ip"}
```

Jamal Ortiz: WAF applied in us-west-1 and eu-west-1. Blocking ~7% of traffic to embeddings; tail latency dropped ~18% in us-west-1 already.

Maria Chen: Good. I'm seeing reduced queue length on embedding workers. But we're still seeing heavy fanout from some IP subnets (44.210.11.0/24).

Ryan Patel: Adding geo/ subnet shape for that /24 to 1r/s:
```
# pseudo config
rate-shaper set --subnet 44.210.11.0/24 --path /v1/embeddings --max-rps 1 --duration 30m --reason "suspected scraper"
```

Support Pager: Notifying affected customers now — template: "We're investigating elevated embedding latency; temporary rate-limiting may affect your requests. We'll update in 30m."

Sofia Rivera: Please add the affected customer IDs: C-8341 (reporting degraded perf), C-1192 (investigating), and C-4420 (noisy tenant but not paying).

Jamal Ortiz: Added temporary key-level blocklist for keys tied to noise. Keys disabled: k_9f3a…, k_2b12… (both flagged by burst pattern).

Maria Chen: We're seeing some retries causing aggregate fanout. Can we enable short-lived 429 backoff header so clients back off more gracefully?

Ryan Patel: Good call — adding Retry-After header on 429 responses and enabling exponential jitter on gateway. Deploying config now.

-- deploy-bot --
deploy-bot: config rollback window opened for 10m; applying gateway change to add Retry-After and 429 jitter.

Ryan Patel: Gateway change applied in canary (10% of traffic) — no errors. Rolling to 50% now.

Maria Chen: Latency improved further on canary. Embedding queue depth down ~45% overall.

Jamal Ortiz: WAF logs show a distinct fingerprint: same Accept-Language, same header order, same Accept-Encoding. We'll add a signature rule and export sample hashes to threat intel.

Sofia Rivera: Support: customers notified. Customer C-8341 replied: "Thanks, please keep us posted — we're in a user demo in 2 hours."

Ryan Patel: Action items: Jamal — escalate WAF signature to blocklist + export for threat intel. Maria — monitor queues and be ready to scale embedding pool if needed. Sofia — follow up with customers at 30m and 60m. I'll keep the quota/canary in place for 30m then evaluate.

Maria Chen: Oncall handoff note for next shift: if traffic returns to normal and latency stays <150ms p50, we can relax quotas. If we see new IP ranges, escalate to sec.

incident-bot: Incident 1951234567 update: mitigations active (WAF, per-key quotas, subnet shaping). Current severity: degraded (service impact to embeddings). Next update in 30m or on notable change.

Support Pager: Logged customer updates at 2026-03-15T18:02Z.

Ryan Patel: Quick post-mortem notes being drafted in /incidents/1951234567-ops-notes — include timeline, keys disabled, WAF rule id scrapper-ua-block-195123, and command snippets.

Jamal Ortiz: FYI we discovered a reseller account programmatically creating keys and distributing them to a scraping operation. We'll need an account level enforcement (KYC flag) and tighter new-key soft limits.

Maria Chen: Agree — add follow-ups: 1) soft-limit new keys to 10 r/s for first 48h, 2) build automated anomaly detection for fanout patterns, 3) add UI/alert for customers with keys showing high request fanout.

Sofia Rivera: I'll create the customer-facing status update draft for legal/comm signoff.

Ryan Patel: Wrapping up for now, sticking to monitoring. If anyone sees escalation, ping @pager. Thanks team.

incident-bot: Incident 1951234567 acknowledged by @Ryan Patel — status: mitigations active.

Support Pager: Last update recorded at 2026-03-15T18:12Z.

Maria Chen: Leaving notes in the thread for handoff — leaving shift in 8m, handing to Jamal.

Jamal Ortiz: Taking over monitoring. Will consolidate logs and open a follow-up ticket for account enforcement.

Sofia Rivera: I'll follow up with affected customers at 18:30Z and attach mitigation summary.

-- end of thread --
